title: Cross-engine — same host, optimized MyVector
subtitle: MyVector (PR #278 NEON) · vsql_vector · pgvector · MariaDB — fashion-mnist-784, all four on one A1 host / identical 4 vCPU · 24 GB
description: The fair, apples-to-apples cross-engine view: optimized MyVector (PR #278 NEON kernels), vsql_vector (VillageSQL), pgvector (Postgres 17), and MariaDB 12.3, all four benchmarked on the same A1 host (each pinned to an identical 4 vCPU / 24 GB slice, run alone), on fashion-mnist-784-euclidean (60k × 784, L2) scored against the dataset's published ground truth. This removes the cross-host confound of the other cross-engine pages (whose non-MyVector engines were measured on the A2 host) and uses MyVector's optimized build — so it answers "where does MyVector actually stand?" honestly. The matched-recall table below is the fair bottom line.
caveats: Why this page exists: the landing, glove and village cross-engine pages measured vsql/pgvector/MariaDB on the A2 host and MyVector's scalar build; mixing hosts/builds is a confound. Here every engine runs on the same A1 host / same 4 vCPU·24 GB slice with MyVector's optimized (PR #278) build — a genuinely unbiased comparison.

The honest read (matched recall@10 — the table above): even with the optimized kernel and same host, pgvector is still ~1.8–2.2× faster than MyVector at recall 0.98–0.995 (it reaches each recall at a much lower ef_search), narrowing to ~1.24× at recall 0.999 (pgvector 539 vs MyVector 434 QPS); MyVector pulls ahead only at the saturated recall-1.0 ceiling (ef=800: 278 vs 162). MariaDB's MHNSW saturates near 1.0 and dominates there (1263 at 0.999). So the kernel fix helped but did NOT close the gap. Looking at recall-per-ef on this same host, the primary cause is recall efficiency, not per-query overhead: pgvector reaches recall 0.99 at ~ef=18 while MyVector needs ~ef=80 (ef=10 recall 0.974 vs 0.934; ef=20 0.993 vs 0.978; they converge by ≥0.998) — so at matched recall MyVector does ~2–4× the distance work. That points at the HNSW graph construction / search quality (or an ef_search-semantics difference between the two implementations) — and it's not just a tunable build parameter: rebuilding at ef_construction=800 (4× the build cost) barely moved MyVector's recall-per-ef (ef=10 0.934→0.943) and stayed well short of pgvector, so the gap is algorithmic. It's a deeper lever than either the distance kernel this PR fixes or the rewrite-path per-query overhead (a smaller secondary factor). The old "~2.4×" figure was scalar MyVector on a different host; removing both confounds, optimized same-host MyVector trails by ~1.2–2× depending on the recall target, mostly for this recall-efficiency reason.

vsql_vector IS included now — a true same-host 4-way: its VillageSQL dev-server (a prebuilt aarch64 tarball) was copied from A2 and run on A1 pinned to the same 4 vCPU slice with a 4 GB InnoDB buffer pool (its default pool thrashed the 188 MB index → a misleading ~2 QPS; with a right-sized pool it builds in 85 s and serves ~1200 QPS at ef=10, matching its A2 behavior). vsql's recall-per-ef tracks pgvector's (ef=10 0.974, ef=20 0.993), so it also reaches a given recall at far lower ef than MyVector — the recall-efficiency gap below is vs both pgvector and vsql.

Dataset / params: fashion-mnist-784-euclidean (ann-benchmarks), HNSW M=16, ef_construction=200 (MyVector + pgvector; MariaDB MHNSW fixes ef_construction at 10). Recall@10 vs published exact neighbors. Warm ef_search sweep; headline cards = warm ef_search=200.

MariaDB builds its HNSW online during insert (its "build" is load time, ~245 s), uses mhnsw_max_cache_size=1 GiB, and floors mhnsw_ef_search to ~2×M so its sub-floor ef=10 point is omitted (kept in the JSON under ef_search_excluded).
Index build: MyVector 46 s vs vsql 85 s vs pgvector 70 s vs MariaDB 245 s — the PR #278 NEON kernels make MyVector's index build the fastest of the four here.
